description: Batch database operations in CrawlResultService.persistResults to eliminate N+1 query pattern
approach: Replace sequential per-item database operations with batch processing: 1) Pre-compute all content hashes and batch query existing records with findMany, 2) Collect new items and use createMany for bulk Prisma inserts, 3) Batch MongoDB document creation, 4) Batch update markdownRef references. This reduces 4N sequential operations to 4 batch operations.

tasks.title: Batch hash computation and existing record lookup
tasks.description: Pre-compute all content hashes upfront and use findMany to batch query existing CrawlResult records instead of individual findFirst calls per item

modification_points.description: Replace loop with individual findFirst to batch hash computation and findMany lookup

implementation: Extract markdown and compute hashes for all items upfront: const itemsWithHash = items.map(item => ({ item, markdown: extractMarkdownResult(item.markdown).primary, hash: hashMarkdown(markdown) })).filter(i => i.markdown)
Collect all hashes: const allHashes = itemsWithHash.map(i => i.hash)
Batch query existing records: const existingRecords = await this.prisma.crawlResult.findMany({ where: { taskId: task.id, contentHash: { in: allHashes } } })
Create lookup Map for O(1) access: const existingMap = new Map(existingRecords.map(r => [r.contentHash, r]))
In processing loop, use Map lookup: const existing = existingMap.get(hash)

unit: Test that findMany is called once with all hashes
Test that Map lookup returns correct existing records
Test that items without markdown are filtered correctly

criteria: Single findMany query replaces N individual findFirst queries
Hash computation happens before any DB operations
Query count reduced from O(n) to O(1) for existence check
All existing functionality preserved (skip duplicates, ingest existing)
verification: Add query logging to verify single findMany call
Measure persistResults time before/after with 50+ items
Run existing crawl tests to verify no regression

commit.message_template: perf(crawl): batch hash lookup in persistResults

tasks.title: Batch create new CrawlResult records
tasks.description: Collect all new CrawlResult records and use createMany instead of individual create calls

modification_points.description: Replace individual create with batch collection and createMany

implementation: Create array to collect new records: const newRecords: Prisma.CrawlResultCreateManyInput[] = []
In loop for non-existing items, push to array instead of immediate create: newRecords.push({ taskId: task.id, sourceUrl, fetchedAt, markdownRef: '', contentHash: hash, metadata })
After loop, execute batch create: const created = await this.prisma.crawlResult.createMany({ data: newRecords, skipDuplicates: true })
Query back created records for IDs: const createdRecords = await this.prisma.crawlResult.findMany({ where: { taskId: task.id, contentHash: { in: newRecords.map(r => r.contentHash) } } })
Create Map for subsequent MongoDB operations: const createdMap = new Map(createdRecords.map(r => [r.contentHash, r]))

unit: Test that createMany is called once with all new records
Test that skipDuplicates prevents constraint violations
Test that created records are correctly mapped back

criteria: Single createMany replaces N individual create calls
New records batch size matches non-duplicate item count
All metadata and fields preserved correctly
No duplicate key errors on race conditions
verification: Verify all new records have correct fields

tasks.title: Batch create MongoDB content documents
tasks.description: Batch MongoDB CrawlResultContentModel.create operations using insertMany

modification_points.description: Replace individual MongoDB create with batch insertMany

implementation: Create array to collect MongoDB documents: const contentDocs: Array<Parameters<typeof CrawlResultContentModel.create>[0]> = []
In loop, push document data to array instead of immediate create
After Prisma batch create, execute MongoDB batch insert: const insertedDocs = await CrawlResultContentModel.insertMany(contentDocs)
Create Map for markdownRef updates: const contentDocMap = new Map(insertedDocs.map((doc, i) => [newRecords[i].contentHash, doc._id.toString()]))

unit: Test that insertMany is called once with all documents
Test that document IDs are correctly mapped back
Test that all fields (markdown, linkAnalysis, tables, media) are preserved

criteria: Single insertMany replaces N individual create calls
All document fields preserved correctly
Document count matches new record count
Media assets processed correctly when storeMedia enabled
verification: Verify all documents have correct resultId references
Test with storeMedia enabled and disabled

commit.message_template: perf(crawl): batch MongoDB content document creation

tasks.title: Batch update markdownRef references
tasks.description: Replace individual Prisma update calls with batch transaction for markdownRef updates

modification_points.description: Replace individual update with batch transaction

implementation: Collect all updates: const markdownRefUpdates = createdRecords.map(r => ({ id: r.id, markdownRef: contentDocMap.get(r.contentHash) }))
Execute batch update in transaction: await this.prisma.$transaction(markdownRefUpdates.map(u => this.prisma.crawlResult.update({ where: { id: u.id }, data: { markdownRef: u.markdownRef } })))
Alternative: Use raw SQL UPDATE with CASE for better performance if update count is high

unit: Test that transaction contains all updates
Test that markdownRef values are correctly set

criteria: Updates batched in single transaction
All markdownRef values correctly linked to MongoDB document IDs
Transaction rollback on any failure
No orphaned records on failure
verification: Verify all CrawlResult records have valid markdownRef

commit.message_template: perf(crawl): batch markdownRef updates in transaction

tasks.title: Batch items ingestion calls
tasks.description: Batch itemsService.createFromCrawlResult calls using Promise.all with concurrency limiting

modification_points.description: Replace sequential itemsService calls with batched parallel execution

implementation: Import p-limit or use custom concurrency limiter: import pLimit from 'p-limit'
Create limiter with reasonable concurrency: const limit = pLimit(10)

Collect all ingest operations: const ingestOps = allResultIds.map(id => limit(() => itemsService.createFromCrawlResult(orgId, userId, id).then(() => ({ success: true, id })).catch(err => ({ success: false, id, error: err }))))
Execute all with Promise.all: const results = await Promise.all(ingestOps)
Count successes and failures: itemsQueued = results.filter(r => r.success).length

unit: Test that Promise.all is used for parallel execution
Test that concurrency is limited to prevent overwhelming
Test that failures are counted correctly

criteria: Items ingestion runs in parallel with concurrency limit
Individual failures don't block other ingestions
Success/failure counts accurate
Total ingestion time reduced by 50%+ for 10+ items

commit.message_template: perf(crawl): parallelize items ingestion with concurrency limit
